sections.title: Intermediate French II
sections.description: French 0400 is the second half of a two-semester intermediate sequence designed to help you attain a level of proficiency that should allow you to function comfortably in a French-speaking environment. You are expected to have already learned the most basic grammatical structures in elementary French and you will review these on your own in the course workbook. This course will build on your existing skills in French, increase your confidence and ability to read, write, speak and understand French, and introduce you to more refined lexical items, more complex grammatical structures, and more challenging cultural material. This course focuses on the culture of French-speaking countries beyond the borders of France. Along with your classmates, you will explore the cities of Dakar, Fort-de-France and Marrakesh, investigating the diversity of the Francophone world through film, literature and music. As in other French courses at Penn, class is conducted entirely in French. In addition to structured oral practice, work in class will include frequent communicative activities such as problem-solving tasks, discussions, and debates, often carried out in pairs or small groups. Daily homework will require researching in the library and on the Internet, listening practice with video clips, in addition to regular written exercises in the workbook.

sections.title: Intermediate French II
sections.description: FREN 0400 is the second half of a two-semester intermediate sequence designed to help you attain a level of proficiency to allow you to function comfortably in a French-speaking environment. You are expected to have already learned the most basic grammatical structures in elementary French. This course invites you to listen to the stories of the French-speaking population outside the borders of France. The figure of the griot, the West African storyteller and guardian of cultural heritage, will be our guide as we learn about the history and traditions of Senegal and Martinique. We will explore the cities of Dakar and Fort-de-France, investigating the diverse perspectives and voices reflected in historical sites, folktales, poetry, film, art, and music. These authentic materials will introduce you to important values and customs, and engage you to consider issues related to identity, the role of education, the influence of Western ideas on non-Western cultures, and the use of oral tradition to preserve cultural heritage. This course is specifically designed to develop your communicative competence as well as your writing and reading skills through the in-depth review and practice of essential grammatical points (past tenses, subjunctive, passive voice, and the passé simple).  Finally, as you listen to the stories from this part of the world, you will have the opportunity to participate in a storytelling project to recount your own personal experiences and preserve the stories that have helped shape the person you are!

This course invites you to listen to the stories of the French-speaking population outside the borders of France. The figure of the griot, the West African storyteller and guardian of cultural heritage, will be our guide as we learn about the history and traditions of Senegal and Martinique. We will explore the cities of Dakar and Fort-de-France, investigating the diverse perspectives and voices reflected in historical sites, folktales, poetry, film, art, and music. These authentic materials will introduce you to important values and customs, and engage you to consider issues related to identity, the role of education, the influence of Western ideas on non-Western cultures, and the use of oral tradition to preserve cultural heritage. This course is specifically designed to develop your communicative competence as well as your writing and reading skills through the in-depth review and practice of essential grammatical points (past tenses, subjunctive, passive voice, and the passé simple).  Finally, as you listen to the stories from this part of the world, you will have the opportunity to participate in a storytelling project to recount your own personal experiences and preserve the stories that have helped shape the person you are!
